rule_tooling_delta.old: A checkpoint report finding must be status "compliant" with evidence and detail.
rule_tooling_delta.new: A successful report finding may be "compliant" or "resolved"; a cited repair with an explanation counts as resolved. Unknown, pending, missing, conflicting, unverified and recorded statuses still block.
rule_tooling_delta.effect: Clears the impossible requirement behind this repository's checkpoint finding: its published reports use "resolved", which alpha.13 could never accept. Upstream cause yolo-dev#40, fixed by publisher PR #59. The finding now reads "Report omits a required semantic rule", which is achievable.
rule_tooling_delta.restriction: Historical reports stay unchanged; failures are cited from a later successful report rather than relabelled.

rule_tooling_delta.old: No request label. Intake reused the source issue; one managed issue is one outcome.
rule_tooling_delta.new: Manifest declares issue_management "request-outcome-v1": a reserved yolo:request label, at most one "## YOLO request" triage comment per classified request, promotion of a source issue in place, many-to-many request/outcome coverage, and a linked Now/Next planning issue when coordination spans outcomes.
rule_tooling_delta.effect: The reserved yolo:request label was created in this repository. Issue #110 is classified after landing, not before, because the old pin governs until then.
rule_tooling_delta.restriction: A request label alone grants no authority, no workflow state and no admission. Only the adopted manifest may require the label; older pins keep their requirements.

rule_tooling_delta.old: A fresh session records loading evidence; the upgrade session cannot attest it and another restart is required.
rule_tooling_delta.new: The observing fresh session may publish its own loading and continuation evidence through separately authorized work in that same session, recording facts under existing write authority.
rule_tooling_delta.effect: Shortens the route to a Q5 observation without changing what counts as evidence.
rule_tooling_delta.restriction: No session may attest a future restart or unobserved continuation; reports are published before any checkpoint is recorded.

rule_tooling_delta.old: No observation contract, setting or executable subcommand.
rule_tooling_delta.new: A new protocol section, an optional adoption "observation" consent, and yolo-check observe emit|query.
rule_tooling_delta.effect: None here. The setting is deliberately absent, which means capture and transmission are off; no adoption field was added and nothing transmits.
rule_tooling_delta.restriction: Opt-in only, separate from feedback consent, failing open, and never a checkpoint or qualification input.

rule_tooling_delta.old: Untagged open issues read "Request open"; nothing records disposition.
rule_tooling_delta.new: Unlabelled or request-only open issues read "Request open" and the panel shows recorded disposition and covering outcomes.
rule_tooling_delta.effect: The status derivation is unchanged and already satisfies the first half; the second half is an unimplemented display, recorded as a limit in ARCHITECTURE.md rather than silently built.
rule_tooling_delta.restriction: Classification alone still proves no review, admission or scheduling.

release_applicability.finding: verification.release.effective_commit had been rewritten three times in published history: 6efd602 (recorded at adoption of the binding), then dbfdacf2 (the v0.3.0 release commit), then 80bf5f86 (the v0.3.1 release commit). The validator compares the current value against every published revision of the marker and requires them all to match.
release_applicability.action_taken: Restored the boundary this repository itself published in .yolo/reports/upgrade-alpha13-proposal.json (release_applicability.effective_commit = 6efd602c6a184320271916d37b6876073d1c546b), and recorded the observed v0.3.1 -> 80bf5f86 mapping that was missing from legacy_tags while already present in .yolo/reports/releases-observed-2026-10-08.json.
release_applicability.probe_result: Both the pinned alpha.13 tool and the candidate alpha.16 tool still report 'Release convention history boundary changed' with that corrected record. Verified by direct probe, not inference.
release_applicability.root_cause: No single current value can satisfy the rule, because Git history contains three different published values and published history is not rewritten: choosing 6efd602 fails against dbfdacf2 and 80bf5f86; choosing 80bf5f86 fails against 6efd602 and dbfdacf2; choosing dbfdacf2 fails against the other two. This is a target record that outgrew a validator assumption, not a repairable local defect.
release_applicability.contradicting_evidence: specs/releases.md (design inputs of this publication) says later migrations preserve established boundaries and identify new requirements in their upgrade evidence, which implies a boundary may be revised. The validator's rule instead requires it never to change once published.
release_applicability.upstream_report: Draft prepared for yolo-dev; not sent. feedback.automatic is false in this adoption, so submission needs explicit maintainer authorization.
release_applicability.earlier_policy: ARCHITECTURE.md has carried a versioning-policy mention since the L1 adoption fa6ec88, before the semver-v1 binding; that earlier mention is not backdated to the convention.

version_repair.decision: Keep package.json#version as the native version source. No version change is part of this migration.
version_repair.rationale: Upgrading the YOLO installation alone does not bump the target product. The alpha.13 migration set 0.1.2 for a future release; releases since then advanced the field normally, so no repair is outstanding.
